name: Question 14
problem:
$$
f(t,z)=⟨3\operatorname{sec}⁡t,\,\text{_____},\,z⟩,\,t\in (-\frac{\pi }{2},\frac{\pi }{2})
$$

The vector-valued function $f(t,z)$ above parametrizes one sheet of the hyperbolic cylinder defined in Cartesian coordinates as $2{x}^{2}-9{y}^{2}=18$ for $x\ge 3.$ What is the second component of $f?$
worked_solution:
Recall that the hyperbola

$$
2{x}^{2}-9{y}^{2}=18\,⇒\,\frac{{x}^{2}}{{3}^{2}}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{(\sqrt{2})^{2}}=1
$$

for $x\ge 3$ in $xy$-plane has the parametrization

$$
⟨x,y⟩=⟨3\operatorname{sec}⁡t,\,\sqrt{2}\operatorname{tan}⁡t⟩,\,t\in (-\frac{\pi }{2},\frac{\pi }{2})
$$

since 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}}{{3}^{2}}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{(\sqrt{2})^{2}} & =\frac{(3\operatorname{sec}⁡t)^{2}}{9}-\frac{(\sqrt{2}\operatorname{tan}⁡t)^{2}}{2} \\  & =\frac{9{sec}^{2}⁡t}{9}-\frac{2{tan}^{2}⁡t}{2} \\  & ={sec}^{2}⁡t-{tan}^{2}⁡t \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, for any point $(x,y,z)$ on our surface, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t,z) & =⟨x,y,z⟩ \\  & =⟨3\operatorname{sec}⁡t,\,\sqrt{2}\operatorname{tan}⁡t,\,z⟩\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\frac{\pi }{2},\frac{\pi }{2})$ and $z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

Therefore, the second component of $f$ is $\sqrt{2}\operatorname{tan}⁡t.$

Question 14
?

f(t,z)=⟨3sec⁡t,_____,z⟩,t∈(−π2,π2)

The vector-valued function f(t,z) above parametrizes one sheet of the hyperbolic cylinder defined in Cartesian coordinates as 2x2−9y2=18 for x≥3. What is the second component of f?

a
2tan⁡t
b
2tan⁡t
c
2csc⁡t
d
2cos⁡t
e
2cos⁡t
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Recall that the hyperbola 2x2−9y2=18⇒x232−y2(2)2=1 for x≥3 in xy-plane has the parametrization ⟨x,y⟩=⟨3sec⁡t,2tan⁡t⟩,t∈(−π2,π2)

since x232−y2(2)2=(3sec⁡t)29−(2tan⁡t)22=9sec2⁡t9−2tan2⁡t2=sec2⁡t−tan2⁡t=1.

Now, for any point (x,y,z) on our surface, we obtain the following: f(t,z)=⟨x,y,z⟩=⟨3sec⁡t,2tan⁡t,z⟩

where t∈(−π2,π2) and z∈(−∞,∞).

Therefore, the second component of f is 2tan⁡t.
